headline: Heterogeneous per-cell knockdown (eta ~ N(1, 0.4)) on k007 priors — fid responds, overall improves to -0.0113
hypotheses_preregistered: Real perturbed cells spread along the delta direction (Atlas-measured eta std ~1.1 median per target); k006/k007 transport fixes eta == 1
Per-cell eta ~ N(1, 0.4), truncated at 0, should improve fid (distribution shape) without hurting signature metrics
next_steps: kd_std sweep (0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7), one submission per day — fid moved but modestly (-0.403 -> -0.388); find the optimum before the mechanism is exhausted
If the sweep plateaus: residual covariance / full Layer B — scalar eta spreads along delta but cannot generate off-direction correlation structure
k009: learned Layer A — context-conditioned K562 -> H1 hESC signature transfer, trained on the Atlas/K562 target overlap
Transport parameter sweep (knockdown_efficiency, attenuation, noise) — held out to avoid leaderboard overfit

provenance.data: VCC 2026 controls + Replogle K562 GWPS bulk + 2025 VCC validation Atlas + STRING v12 neighbor map (k007)

log: k007 priors unchanged (dispatch real 816 / neighbor 54 / fallback 30); only the sampler changed: perturbed_i = basal_i + eta_i * delta + eps, eta ~ N(1, 0.4) clipped at 0, eps ~ N(0, 0.05). Overall -0.0159 -> -0.0113. fid improved modestly (-0.403 -> -0.388), nmae +0.002 -> +0.007, pds 0.269 -> 0.272. Hypothesis partially confirmed: scalar KD heterogeneity is real signal but small — it models spread along the delta axis only. The residual fid deficit likely lives in off-direction covariance, which needs the full Layer B sampler.
